section_1.title: The Problem: Information Overload
section_1.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs) which struggle with long-range dependencies. Define 'Attention' as the ability to selectively focus on relevant parts of input.
section_1.example: Reading a long mystery novel: You don't memorize every word; you focus on the clues that link the detective to the culprit.

section_2.title: The Core Components: Query, Key, and Value
section_2.content: Explain the Q, K, V retrieval system using an analogy to a library database. Visual: Query (what I want), Key (the labels on the book spines), Value (the content inside).
section_2.example: A library search: Your search term (Query) is compared against book titles (Keys) to retrieve the most useful information (Values).

section_3.title: Calculating Relevance: Dot Product & Softmax
section_3.content: Introduce the mathematical intuition: Score = (Query · Key) / sqrt(d). Use a heat map graphic to show how similar items get higher weights, then 'Softmax' turns these into probabilities (percentages).
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'focus matrix': If the word is 'Apple', the matrix shows a bright 'red' spot on 'fruit' and a 'dim' spot on 'jump'.

section_4.title: Bringing it Together: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
section_4.content: Combine the concepts: Multiply the weights by the Values to get a 'weighted sum.' This is the final vector representation that the model 'understands'.
section_4.example: Imagine a chef choosing ingredients: The weight (Attention) determines how much salt or spice (Value) goes into the final dish based on the recipe (Query).

section_5.title: Application: Multi-Head Attention
section_5.content: Explain that Transformers run multiple 'attention' processes in parallel to capture different types of relationships simultaneously (grammar, sentiment, context).
section_5.example: A team of researchers: One person focuses on the historical facts, another on the emotional tone, and a third on the scientific logic—all synthesizing one final summary.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Query asks what I need.", "Key acts as a label.", "Value provides the actual content."]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Components: Q, K, and V", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define assets
        q_box = Square(color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.5)
        k_box = Square(color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.5)
        v_box = Square(color="#3357FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        q_label = Text("Q", font_size=24, color="#FF5733").next_to(q_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        k_label = Text("K", font_size=24, color="#33FF57").next_to(k_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=24, color="#3357FF").next_to(v_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Magnifying glass
        magnifier = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE).add(Text("🔍", font_size=20))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(q_box, q_label), "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(k_box, k_label), "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v_box, v_label), "B6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(VGroup(q_box, q_label, k_box, k_label, v_box, v_label)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(magnifier, "B4")
        self.play(Create(magnifier))
        self.play(magnifier.animate.shift(0.5*DOWN), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        v_final = v_box.copy().set_fill(opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(v_final, "E4")
        self.play(Transform(v_box.copy(), v_final))
        self.wait(2)

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
